title.narrative: Land, Water and Peace: Institutional and community empowerment and peacebuilding through sustainable natural resources management and resilient livelihoods in Cabo Delgado, Mozambique

description.narrative:
The ongoing armed conflict in Cabo Delgado, Northern Mozambique, has persisted for over five years, leading to widespread destruction, human rights abuses, and mass displacement. Since 2017, attacks by Non-State Armed Groups (NSAGs) have escalated, spreading into neighboring provinces, displacing over 834,000 people, and exacerbating poverty, food insecurity, and social instability. Government and international military efforts have regained some control, but sporadic attacks continue to hinder humanitarian assistance and development efforts.
In response, the Mozambican government launched key initiatives such as the Plano de Reconstrução de Cabo Delgado (PRCD) and the Northern Mozambique Resilience and Integrated Development Programme (PREDIN) to restore stability, rebuild infrastructure, and support displaced communities. These programs align with broader national and international frameworks, including the UN Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework and the Peacebuilding Fund (PBF), to address the root causes of conflict poverty, inequality, and competition over land and natural resources.
The proposed project focuses on promoting social cohesion, peace, and sustainable natural resource management by improving access to land and water for displaced populations, returnees, and host communities. Through participatory planning, capacity building, and infrastructure development, the initiative aims to:
Enhance participatory governance by incorporating the needs of affected communities into natural resource management. Improve livelihoods and social cohesion through sustainable land and water use, infrastructure projects, and climate-smart agricultural practices.
Strengthen institutional frameworks to support inclusive decision-making and prevent future conflicts over natural resources. A gender-responsive, community-led approach will ensure equitable access to resources, economic empowerment for vulnerable groups particularly women and long-term resilience for conflict-affected populations. By integrating humanitarian assistance with development efforts, the project aims to facilitate durable solutions for displacement, support local economies, and contribute to lasting peace in Northern Mozambique.
